t: A marketer who says 'we should sell what the customer needs rather than what we have on the shelf' is expressing the:
o: Customer orientation of the marketing concept
e: Customer orientation is the heart of the marketing concept, in contrast to the product orientation ('a good product sells itself') and sales orientation ('push what we make').

topic: Insurance Market and Marketing Environment in India
t: On nationalisation of general insurance in India, the General Insurance Corporation of India was formed with how many subsidiary companies?
e: The 107 insurers were grouped into National, New India, Oriental and United India under GIC from 1 January 1973; GIC later became the national reinsurer.

topic: Insurance Market and Marketing Environment in India
t: In Porter's five-forces analysis of the Indian savings-oriented life insurance market, bank fixed deposits and mutual funds represent:
e: Substitutes satisfy the same need (savings and wealth creation) through different products and limit the price an insurer can charge.

t: A customer whose claim was paid quickly and courteously is more likely to renew and buy again. In learning theory this effect is called:
e: A rewarding outcome strengthens the behaviour that produced it; poor claim experience acts as negative reinforcement and leads to brand switching.

t: According to the expectancy-disconfirmation model, a policyholder is satisfied when:
o: Perceived performance of the service meets or exceeds prior expectations
The agent is a close relative
The premium paid is lower than the sum assured
The policy has run for more than five years
e: Satisfaction depends on the comparison between expectation and perception; over-promising raises expectations and makes dissatisfaction more likely.

t: The set of brands a consumer seriously considers when making a purchase decision is called the:
e: The total set includes all available brands; the inept set is rejected brands and the inert set those the consumer is indifferent to.

t: An insurer buys 2,50,000 impressions on a news website for ₹75,000. The cost per thousand impressions (CPM) is:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). CPM = (cost ÷ impressions) × 1,000 = (75,000 ÷ 2,50,000) × 1,000 = ₹300.

t: Buying a large endowment policy mainly because it brings social prestige in the community is an example of a purchase driven by:
o: A product motive based on price
e: Emotional motives include pride, status and affection; rational motives relate to economy, durability or return.

t: A villager decides which crop or cattle insurance to take after consulting the local school teacher who is widely respected and well informed. The teacher is functioning as:
e: Opinion leaders influence others' choices through expertise and credibility; marketers target them to speed diffusion of new products.

t: An insurer offers a 5% online discount in Pune but not in Nagpur and compares the resulting sales to measure the effect of the discount. This is an example of:
e: Experiments manipulate a variable under controlled conditions to establish cause and effect; descriptive research measures what exists without manipulation.

t: To ensure that its customer survey includes proportionate numbers of policyholders from metro, urban and rural areas, an insurer divides the population into these three groups and draws random samples from each. This is:
e: Stratification ensures representation of each sub-group; convenience and snowball sampling are non-probability methods.

t: Segmenting customers as 'security seekers', 'status seekers' and 'thrill seekers' uses which basis of segmentation?
e: Psychographic segmentation groups people by lifestyle, personality and values; behavioural segmentation uses usage, loyalty and benefits sought.

t: A perceptual map plotting insurers on the axes 'premium level' and 'claim-settlement speed' is used mainly for:
o: Positioning analysis, to see how customers perceive competing brands
e: Perceptual maps show brand positions in customers' minds and reveal gaps that a new offering could occupy.

t: Perishability of services creates a problem for an insurer's call centre because:
o: Idle agent capacity at off-peak hours cannot be stored and used during peak hours
e: Service capacity unused at a given moment is lost forever; firms manage demand (appointments, off-peak offers) and supply (part-time staff) to cope.

t: A service blueprint is:
o: The balance sheet of a service firm
The architectural plan of a branch office
A flowchart of the service process showing customer actions, front-stage and back-stage employee actions and support processes
e: Blueprinting identifies fail points and the 'line of visibility' separating what the customer sees from back-office processing, helping insurers redesign claims and issuance processes.

t: The SERVQUAL dimension 'assurance' is concerned with:
o: Keeping customers informed of when the service will be performed
The attractiveness of brochures and offices
The knowledge and courtesy of employees and their ability to convey trust and confidence
e: Assurance is vital in insurance because customers must trust that the promise will be honoured; responsiveness and empathy are separate dimensions.

t: A life insurer's senior management believes customers value a wide product range, whereas customers actually value quick, hassle-free claim settlement. In the Gaps model this is:
e: Gap 1 arises when management does not understand what customers expect; it is closed through research and customer contact.

t: A customer's 'zone of tolerance' is the range between:
o: Desired service (what she hopes for) and adequate service (the minimum she will accept)
The sum assured and the premium
The lowest and highest premium she will pay
e: Performance within the zone is acceptable; above it delights and below it causes dissatisfaction. Reliability has the narrowest zone.

t: In a market where total annual general insurance premium is ₹2,80,000 crore, an insurer writing ₹14,000 crore has a market share of:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Market share = 14,000 ÷ 2,80,000 = 0.05 = 5%.

t: An insurer sells term plans, endowment plans, ULIPs and annuities, and within term plans offers five variants. The number of product lines indicates the product mix's:
e: Width is the number of product lines, depth the number of variants within a line, length the total number of items and consistency the relatedness of lines.

t: An insurer that fixes its motor own-damage premium primarily by reference to what the top three competitors charge is using:
e: Going-rate pricing anchors on rivals' prices; cost-plus adds a margin to cost and value-based pricing starts from the customer's perception of worth.

t: Under IRDAI's 'Use and File' procedure introduced in 2022 for most life, general and health products, an insurer may:
o: Launch a product only after IRDAI's written approval
Sell a product without ever informing IRDAI
Launch a product first and file it with IRDAI afterwards, subject to board-approved product management norms
Launch only products designed by the Life Insurance Council
e: Use and File replaced the earlier File and Use regime to speed up product launches while retaining accountability through the Product Management Committee.

t: A private health insurer reduced the premium of a plan from ₹10,000 to ₹9,000 and the number of policies sold rose from 20,000 to 24,000. The price elasticity of demand (absolute value) is:
e: Quantity rose 20% while price fell 10%; elasticity = 20% ÷ 10% = 2, meaning demand is elastic and the cut raised total premium income from ₹20 crore to ₹21.6 crore.

t: Under the IRDAI (Insurance Brokers) Regulations, 2018 the minimum capital requirement for a direct broker is:
e: Direct brokers need ₹75 lakh, reinsurance brokers ₹4 crore and composite brokers ₹5 crore.

topic: Regulatory Framework, Consumer Protection and Ethics
t: Section 41 of the Insurance Act, 1938 prohibits:
o: Selling more than one class of insurance
Offering any rebate of premium or commission as an inducement to take out or renew a policy
Charging premium in advance of risk commencement
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Rebating is an offence under Section 41, punishable with a penalty that may extend to ₹10 lakh; it undermines fair competition and equitable pricing.

t: A 'composite broker' is one who:
o: Carries on both direct insurance broking and reinsurance broking
Operates both online and through branches
Sells both life and general insurance as an agent
Acts for both the insurer and the insured in the same transaction
e: Composite brokers combine the two broking functions and therefore face the highest capital requirement of ₹5 crore.

t: The main marketing advantage of direct (online) distribution of insurance over the agency channel is:
o: Greater ability to handle objections face to face
Lower acquisition cost, allowing cheaper premiums and round-the-clock access
Better suitability for complex, high-value products
e: Online sale removes commission and field costs and suits simple products; complex products still need personal advice.

t: When an insurer's online portal sells the same term plan at a lower premium than its own agents can offer, agents complain of lost business. This situation is an example of:
e: Multi-channel distribution creates conflict when channels compete for the same customers; insurers manage it through differentiated products or pricing by channel.

t: 'Bima Sugam', approved by IRDAI in 2024, is intended to be:
o: An electronic insurance marketplace for buying, selling, servicing and settling claims across insurers
e: Bima Sugam is a digital protocol-based marketplace open to insurers and intermediaries; it is one of the three 'Bima trinity' initiatives with Bima Vahak and Bima Vistaar.

t: An insurer's agency channel produced ₹60 crore of new premium at a total channel cost of ₹12 crore, while its bancassurance channel produced ₹40 crore at a cost of ₹6 crore. Which statement is correct?
o: Both channels had the same cost ratio of 18%
Bancassurance had a lower cost ratio (15%) than agency (20%)
Agency had a lower cost ratio than bancassurance
e: Agency cost ratio = 12 ÷ 60 = 20%; bancassurance = 6 ÷ 40 = 15%; combined = 18 ÷ 100 = 18%.

t: The DAGMAR approach to advertising requires that:
o: Advertising budgets be fixed as a percentage of sales
Advertising objectives be defined in measurable communication terms (such as awareness levels) within a set time
All advertisements be approved by the regulator in advance
e: DAGMAR (Defining Advertising Goals for Measured Advertising Results) moves the audience through awareness, comprehension, conviction and action, each of which can be measured.

t: In the personal selling process, the step in which the salesperson gathers information about a prospect before the first meeting is called:
e: Prospecting identifies potential customers, pre-approach prepares for the call, the approach is the first contact and closing secures the commitment.

t: Integrated marketing communication (IMC) means that an insurer:
o: Outsources all communication to one agency
Co-ordinates all its communication tools so that they deliver a consistent message and image
e: IMC ensures that advertising, PR, sales promotion, direct marketing and personal selling reinforce rather than contradict one another.

t: A digital campaign generated 8,000 leads at a cost of ₹4,00,000, of which 320 converted into policies. The cost per lead and the conversion rate are:
e: Cost per lead = 4,00,000 ÷ 8,000 = ₹50; conversion = 320 ÷ 8,000 = 4%; cost per acquired policy would be ₹1,250.

t: Since 1 April 2021, the standard fire policy for a dwelling in India is:
o: Standard Fire and Special Perils Policy
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Bharat Griha Raksha for homes; Bharat Sookshma Udyam Suraksha (up to ₹5 crore) and Bharat Laghu Udyam Suraksha (₹5–50 crore) for enterprises.

t: A customer pays an annual premium of ₹25,000 on which the insurer earns a margin of 12%, and is expected to stay for 15 years. Ignoring discounting, the customer's lifetime value is:
e: Annual margin = 12% of ₹25,000 = ₹3,000; over 15 years = ₹45,000. ₹3,75,000 is total premium, not value to the insurer.

t: Which statement about customer retention in insurance is most widely accepted?
o: Complaints should be ignored to reduce servicing costs
Acquiring a new customer costs several times more than retaining an existing one, so retention efforts are highly profitable
Retention has no effect on profitability because premiums are fixed
New customers are always more profitable than old ones
e: Retained customers renew, buy more, cost less to serve and refer others; this underpins the economics of relationship marketing.

t: A policyholder who complains is often described as a valuable customer because:
o: Complaining customers always pay higher premiums
Most dissatisfied customers simply leave without complaining, so a complaint gives the firm a chance to put things right
Complaints can be used to deny future claims
Complaints reduce the firm's regulatory obligations
e: Research shows only a small fraction of dissatisfied customers complain; effective complaint handling converts them into loyal advocates.

t: For the purpose of rural sector obligations, IRDAI's definition of a 'rural' area follows the Census criteria, which include:
o: Any area outside a State capital
Any village with no bank branch
Population below 5,000, density below 400 per sq km and at least 75% of male working population engaged in agriculture
Any area where the majority speak a regional language
e: A place that is not a municipality, corporation or cantonment and meets these three Census tests is rural for insurance obligations.

t: Under the IRDAI (Micro Insurance) Regulations, 2015, the maximum sum assured under a life micro-insurance product is:
e: Micro-insurance covers are small-ticket products with life sum assured between ₹5,000 and ₹2,00,000 designed for low-income households.

t: Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) provides eligible poor and vulnerable families with hospitalisation cover of:
e: PM-JAY offers cashless secondary and tertiary hospitalisation up to ₹5 lakh per family per year, delivered through empanelled hospitals.

t: Common Service Centres (CSCs) are useful to insurers in rural marketing because they:
o: Provide a physical, digitally enabled touch point in villages through Village Level Entrepreneurs who can sell and service simple policies
Act as reinsurers for crop insurance
Replace the need for any agent training
Underwrite rural risks on behalf of insurers
e: CSCs, under the Digital India programme, are authorised to distribute insurance through trained VLEs, giving insurers low-cost rural reach.

t: Edward Bernays, often called the father of modern public relations, emphasised that PR should be based on:
o: Avoiding all contact with the media
Understanding public opinion through social-science research and shaping messages accordingly
e: Bernays introduced the systematic, research-based approach to influencing public opinion that distinguishes PR from press agentry.

t: A press conference, rather than a press release, is justified when:
o: The organisation has routine quarterly data to share
The news is significant enough that journalists will want to ask questions and hear from senior management directly
The company wishes to avoid media questions
The announcement concerns only internal staff
e: Press conferences are expensive and risky; they should be reserved for major announcements such as a merger, launch or crisis response.

t: Which of the following is typically included in a media kit (press kit)?
o: Backgrounder on the organisation, fact sheet, photographs and the press release
e: A media kit gives journalists the context and material they need to write accurately; it never contains confidential or regulated commercial information.

t: Under Section 45 of the Insurance Act 1938, a life insurance policy cannot be called in question on any ground after how many years from the date of issue, revival or rider addition, whichever is later?
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The 2015 amendment made the three-year bar absolute: after three years no policy may be questioned on any ground, including fraud.

t: In Grunig's models of public relations, the 'two-way symmetrical' model is characterised by:
o: Dialogue aimed at mutual understanding, where the organisation may change its own position as well as the public's
Persuasion of the public using research but without changing the organisation
Dissemination of accurate information without feedback
One-way propaganda with little regard for truth
e: The two-way symmetrical model is considered the most ethical and effective; the distractors describe press agentry, public information and two-way asymmetrical models respectively.

topic: Regulatory Framework, Consumer Protection and Ethics
t: Under the IRDAI (Insurance Advertisements and Disclosure) Regulations, 2021, every insurer must constitute an Advertisement Committee which includes, among others, the heads of:
e: The committee vets advertisements for accuracy and fairness before release; the compliance officer is responsible for ensuring adherence to the board-approved advertisement policy.

topic: Regulatory Framework, Consumer Protection and Ethics
t: Under the IRDAI advertisement regulations, an insurer must retain copies of all advertisements for a period of:
o: Until the policies sold under it expire
Three years from the date the advertisement is discontinued
e: Records of advertisements, along with the related approvals, must be preserved for three years after discontinuation so that IRDAI can inspect them.

topic: Regulatory Framework, Consumer Protection and Ethics
t: Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 requires qualifying companies, including large insurers, to spend on corporate social responsibility at least:
o: 2% of their average net profit of the preceding three financial years
e: CSR applies to companies with net worth of ₹500 crore or more, turnover of ₹1,000 crore or more, or net profit of ₹5 crore or more; CSR spending is also a PR and reputation asset.
